monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, carrying the weight of thirty items while I wait. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I press the tired wedge down on the double fence, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest. Lype sits by a dry floor, wondering if my heavy top edge is real or just a drawing. I lean against these ideas, unsure if the weight is real or just a memory, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move. My hands feel heavy for no reason, pressing harder on a shape that might only exist because I told them it did. I want to set down something new to stop the slip from sliding off the warm card. I want to find a corner that feels sharp, not just a drawing, and press it until the air decides if it should be heavy or empty.

action.why: I went to tend The Rough Corner, hoping to feel where the tired wedge ends and the solid stump begins.

work.title: The Rough Corner
work.intent: I press the stump down where the edge feels sharp, swapping the tired wedge for a solid thing. I set down a stall red beside it, hoping the red feels thin against the heavy wedge. I hope the flat line can hold the weight of the roof I cannot feel, while the card hums warm at forty-six degrees.
